name: Abfaltersbach
kurzbeschreibung: Charming village in the Pustertal with traditional Osttiroler farmhouses and stunning mountain views.
beschreibung:
Overview

Abfaltersbach is situated at an elevation of 983 meters in the sunny Hochpustertal valley of East Tyrol, nestled between the Villgraten Mountains to the north and the jagged peaks of the Lienz Dolomites to the south. With approximately 650 residents, the municipality in the district of Lienz offers an authentic alpine setting marked by preserved rural tranquility and scenic beauty. The community encompasses the main village alongside the picturesque hamlets of Abfaltern, Einöd, Geselhaus, and Walde. The Drau River flows gently through the valley floor, accompanied by the scenic Drau Cycle Path. Far from mass tourism, Abfaltersbach charms visitors with its friendly village life, traditional wooden architecture, and peaceful meadows.

History

Settlement in the valley dates back to the early medieval era: as early as 769 AD, Duke Tassilo III of Bavaria mentioned the local Erlbach stream as a boundary marker in the foundation charter of Innichen Abbey. The village was officially documented in 973 under the name Affulturpach, a reference to wild apple trees or elder groves lining the streams. For centuries, this watercourse served as the geopolitical border between the County of Gorizia and the Prince-Bishopric of Freising and Brixen. Following the extinction of the Counts of Gorizia in 1500, Emperor Maximilian I integrated the valley into Habsburg Tyrol. The Gothic parish church of Saint Andrew was consecrated in 1441 and refurbished with exquisite Rococo elements in 1765.

Getting There

By car from Innsbruck, motorists travel via the Brenner Motorway A13 into South Tyrol and follow the Pustertal road SS49 past Bruneck and Innichen, reaching Abfaltersbach in approximately two hours. An all-Austrian route travels via Kitzbühel, the Felbertauern Tunnel, and Lienz along the B100 in two and a half hours. From Munich, the most direct access leads via Kufstein and the Felbertauern. By rail, Abfaltersbach station is located on the Drau Valley railway, featuring hourly regional trains between Lienz and Innichen. In addition, the VVT RegiobusExpress line 960X operates daily direct coach connections from Innsbruck Central Station to Abfaltersbach village center.

Tips

A unique historic attraction is the heritage-protected Aigner Badl in Einöd, the last operating historic farm spa in East Tyrol. Guests can enjoy soothing baths in original larch-wood tubs fed by a calcium-sulfate healing spring established in 1772. The parish church of Saint Andrew in Abfaltern features impressive Rococo ceiling frescoes by Josef Anton Zoller and a dramatic 15th-century mural of Saint Christopher. Hikers should explore the scenic trail up to the Schönfeldalm at 1,981 meters, segments of the East Tyrolean Camino de Santiago, and the panoramic Pustertal High Road. The gentle Drau Cycle Path provides easy cycling toward Lienz. Local taverns serve delicious Schlipfkrapfen dumplings and aromatic Pregler fruit brandy.
